newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Mar 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Mar 19.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- TA KUNG PAO -- Hong Kong media visited the base in Shantou of marines attached to the People's Liberation Army's Hong Kong garrison. The unit had been well prepared to come to the territory in smooth order.
-- SING TAO DAILY -- Sources said imprisoned Chinese dissident Wang Dang had accepted an offer from authorities for him to leave the country after his release, which was expected to come soon.
-- MING PAO -- Taiwan passed a law regulating its relations with Hong Kong and Macau, a copy of which would be sent to the future Chief Executive, Tung Chee-hwa.

-- A prominent Taiwanese writer said that some people in Taiwan refused to acknowledge that they were Chinese, unwilling to read Chinese history or speak Mandarin. Some even suggested treating Chinese literature as part of "foreign literature".
-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- The flotation of red-chip candidate GITIC Enterprises was thrown into serious doubt yesterday by the intervention of China's securties regulators.
-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Five men arrested in the Independence Commission Against Corruption's probe into a horse racing scandal had been charged with illegal gambling.
-- China's largest computer maker, Legend Group, had signed a landmark agreement worth more than 100 million yuan with Microsoft Corp to install Windows 95 in its computers.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- The advance party of marines of the People's Liberation Army Hong Kong garrison would not be armed, and no Chinese naval vessels would be sent to Hong Kong before the handover.
-- President Jiang Zemin faced critical challenges from both the left and right of the Communist Party immediately after the funeral of the late patriarch Deng Xiaoping.
